newsitem.title: CHINA: China tries to hold antimony at $2,300/T - traders.
newsitem.headline: China tries to hold antimony at $2,300/T - traders.

text.p: Chinese antimony producers are trying to hold sagging prices of the strategic metal at around $2,300 a tonne FOB, industry officials said on Monday.
"Antimony has been selling for $2,300 to $2,400 a tonne over the last couple days," an official of the China National Non-ferrous Metals Import and Export Corp said.
"Supply has now far outstripped demand on the international market," he said.
The All China Antimony Producer's Association earlier this year set a fourth quarter floor price of 21,500 yuan ($2,590).
Another official with the China National Non-ferrous Metals Industry Corp said producers have been unable to stop antimony's slide.
"Whatever price they try to set isn't important -- what's important is will the market accept that price," he said.
China produced 91,200 tonnes of antimony in 1995 and official forecasts have said output of the silvery-white chemical element used to harden alloys could reach 100,000 tonnes this year.
Ths country is working hard to cut output of antimony, the Import and Export Corp official said.
China has already closed many small antimony plants in a bid to reduce output to stabilise world prices and cut pollution.
Antimony peaked in late 1994 at $6,000 a tonne.
